name: term-cancel
how: emphasize the vanishing terms (highlight color), then fade them, then write the simplified result below — communicates algebraic reduction as a visible event, not a hidden step

name: reveal-answer-first
how: write the final result centered and large, pause, then fade it to a corner while the proof elements are drawn in — signals 'we know where we are going' before the journey begins

name: invariant-banner
how: write a labeled equation (e.g. 'brightness = π²/4') at a fixed top or bottom position, pause to let it register, and leave it on screen untouched through all subsequent draw operations — holds the preserved quantity in peripheral view

name: zone-split
how: draw a vertical line dividing the stage, plot a diagram on the left and write its algebraic counterpart on the right, keeping both visible simultaneously — lets geometry and formula confirm each other without switching scenes

name: nested-reference
how: draw a small circle, pause, then plot a larger circle around it; when the outer circle reaches limiting scale replace it with a line — shows a geometric limit as a sequence of concrete draw operations rather than an abstract statement

name: label-then-drop
how: write a term label with an arrow pointing into a formula, pause, then fade the label while leaving the formula's color unchanged — names a part exactly once, then trusts persistent color to carry meaning forward

name: false-cross-replace
how: write the incorrect claim, draw an X line through it, then replace it with the corrected version in the same position — makes the distinction spatial and immediate rather than verbal

name: closing-loop
how: fade all current elements, redraw the opening object or question from the first scene, then write new vocabulary or result beside it — gives the viewer explicit conceptual closure by returning to where they started

name: step-path-walk
how: draw the first vector or segment, pause, then draw the next segment starting from its endpoint, adding an arrow at each joint — turns coordinate addition into felt, sequential movement rather than a static sum

name: emphasis-isolate
how: fade all elements except one target, emphasize that element (thicken or pulse via emphasize op), write a brace or label beside it, pause — pulls one factor out of visual noise so the audience focuses before the explanation begins

name: numeric-converge
how: write a decimal approximation, replace it with a closer one, replace again, then replace with the exact symbolic constant highlighted — lets numbers do persuasion before the algebraic proof arrives

name: mini-top-band
how: draw scaled-down copies of the main diagram in a row along the top edge with vertical separator lines, leaving the main stage free — keeps the global structure visible while the detail is being built below
